question: Which brain chemical is severely lacking in Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Serotonin

explanation: Parkinson's disease specifically results from the death of neurons that produce dopamine in a part of the midbrain called the substantia nigra. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four parts of Deming's System of Profound Knowledge?

options.A: Knowledge of variation
options.B: Psychology
options.C: Financial accounting
options.D: Theory of knowledge

explanation: The four pillars are: system appreciation, variation, theory of knowledge, and psychology. Financial accounting is important business stuff, but not part of this specific framework!

question: Why do nurse researchers study a smaller sample instead of the whole population?

options.A: Hospital ethics committees forbid studying more than ten patients
options.B: It is usually impossible or impractical to study every single person
options.C: Sampling guarantees that zero errors will occur during data collection
options.D: Patients refuse to answer research questions if the group is too large

explanation: You got it! Imagine trying to interview every single diabetic patient in Nigeria—it's way too much work and time. That's why we use a manageable sample.

question: Why should a nurse researcher investigate an outlier rather than deleting it immediately?

options.A: Outliers always improve the accuracy of statistical tests
options.B: It proves that the measurement scale was ordinal
options.C: Deleting data is illegal in all health research
options.D: It might represent a genuine, important clinical finding

explanation: An extreme value might look like an error at first glance, but it could actually reflect a real, critical clinical event that deserves attention. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which antenatal care service is most crucial for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: Intensive nutritional counseling and iron supplementation
options.B: Mandatory enrollment in adult literacy classes
options.C: Immediate scheduling of elective tubal ligation
options.D: Restriction of physical activity throughout all trimesters

explanation: Because teen moms are still growing and easily get anemic, good nutrition guidance and iron supplements are absolute top priorities.

question: In public health, what does the term 'herd immunity' mean?

options.A: The body builds resistance to infections through natural dietary intake
options.B: High vaccination rates in a community protect vulnerable unvaccinated people
options.C: White blood cells group together to surround and isolate a foreign microbe
options.D: Animals transmit specific infectious diseases directly to human populations

explanation: Herd immunity is teamwork at a community level! When almost everyone is vaccinated, the disease has nowhere to travel, shielding babies and vulnerable neighbors who can't take vaccines.

question: Why is it so important to involve the community in disaster risk reduction?

options.A: Government policies mandate that citizens handle disasters without any professional help
options.B: Community members can legally replace trained national fire fighters
options.C: Local residents provide all the heavy financial grants needed for rebuilding
options.D: Residents understand their local hazards and are more likely to practice safety habits they helped plan

explanation: That's right! When locals help plan safety measures, they know the area best and are much more likely to actually follow through with them.

question: Why is watching closely for signs of infection so important for patients on chemotherapy?

options.A: Patients are unable to take oral fluids during chemotherapy treatment
options.B: Surgery automatically destroys the lymphatic system permanently
options.C: Chemotherapy lowers the white blood cell count, making the body vulnerable to pathogens
options.D: Ovarian tumors produce bacteria that multiply rapidly in the bloodstream

explanation: Brilliant! Chemotherapy temporarily slows down bone marrow function, leaving the patient with fewer white blood cells to fight off germs.

question: A nurse is working in a crowded emergency shelter after a flood. What is the most important step to prevent a disease outbreak?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on major surgical procedures on-site
options.B: Ensuring access to safe drinking water and maintaining sanitation
options.C: Conducting formal structural engineering tests on the shelter
options.D: Refusing admission to anyone showing signs of mild stress

explanation: In crowded shelters, poor hygiene and unsafe water can easily cause disease outbreaks. Clean water and sanitation are your best defenses here! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h8)

question: What happens inside the eye of a person with cataracts?

options.A: The natural lens becomes cloudy and blocks clear light
options.B: The macula breaks down and destroys central vision
options.C: Intraocular pressure rises and damages the optic nerve
options.D: Tiny blood vessels on the retina burst and bleed

explanation: Cataracts are characterized by the opacification or clouding of the eye's natural lens, which blurs the incoming light. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: What happens to the color absorption properties of hemoglobin when it binds with oxygen?

options.A: It absorbs more red light and less infrared light
options.B: It absorbs more infrared light and less red light
options.C: It turns the surrounding plasma completely dark blue
options.D: It stops absorbing all types of light completely

explanation: Oxygenated hemoglobin absorbs infrared light differently than deoxygenated hemoglobin, which allows the oximeter sensor to measure the ratio. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which Nigerian government bodies coordinate national and state-level disaster management?

options.A: EFCC and ICPC
options.B: NEPA and PHCN
options.C: JAMB and WAEC
options.D: NEMA and SEMA

explanation: Good to know for your community health postings! NEMA handles things at the national level, while SEMA takes charge at the state level.

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness (BPCR) during antenatal care?

options.A: To train family members to deliver the baby at home safely
options.B: To prevent dangerous delays in reaching emergency obstetric care
options.C: To remove the financial cost of hospital supplies completely
options.D: To guarantee that the baby is born on the exact estimated date

explanation: BPCR is all about planning ahead (transport, funds, blood donors) so that if an emergency strikes, the mother doesn't lose precious time.

question: Which food group is the body's main and quickest source of energy?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Fats
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs break down quickly into glucose, which acts as the favorite fuel for your cells and brain.

question: What does the term 'orthostatic hypotension' mean?

options.A: A sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up
options.B: Swelling in the lower legs due to poor circulation
options.C: A spike in heart rate after eating heavy meals
options.D: High blood pressure caused by sleeping flat on the back

explanation: When blood vessels are slow to adjust to a new position, standing up too fast can cause a dizzy spell because of a sudden drop in pressure. Good to know for patient safety!

question: What is the purpose of recommending pelvic floor exercises in the long-term recovery phase?

options.A: To help restore and strengthen anal sphincter tone
options.B: To speed up the healing of abdominal skin scars
options.C: To increase the production of digestive enzymes
options.D: To prevent the development of high blood pressure

explanation: Strengthening the pelvic floor muscles improves overall continence and pelvic support after surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h9)

question: What causes the sudden symptoms of Katayama fever (acute schistosomiasis)?

options.A: The immediate accumulation of snail toxins inside the human bloodstream
options.B: A secondary bacterial infection entering through skin puncture sites
options.C: The migration and development of immature worms through tissues
options.D: The sudden death of adult worms inside the intestinal lumen

explanation: Katayama fever is basically your immune system throwing a fit as young worms travel through your body tissues and blood. Your body is fighting hard!

question: What is the main job of the tough outer shell (exoskeleton) on an insect?

options.A: Generating body heat during cold weather
options.B: Pumping oxygen directly into the insect bloodstream
options.C: Protecting internal organs and preventing water loss
options.D: Producing venom to paralyze small prey

explanation: That crunchy outer coat acts like a suit of armor that keeps the insect safe and stops it from drying out in the sun.

question: A nurse identifies a case of polio. Why do we place polio in a special, urgent reporting category?

options.A: It is a targeted disease for global eradication and elimination
options.B: It only affects elderly patients in urban hospitals
options.C: It is a common seasonal allergy with mild symptoms
options.D: It does not require tracking by government agencies

explanation: The world is actively trying to wipe out polio completely. Because every single case is a global emergency, we track them with extreme urgency!

question: What do we call an overactive immune response that leads to allergic symptoms or tissue damage?

options.A: Autoagglutination
options.B: Immunodeficiency
options.C: Immunotolerance
options.D: Hypersensitivity

explanation: Hypersensitivity is simply an exaggerated immune reaction to things that are normally harmless, like pollen or certain foods.

question: How can a nurse best support a burnt-out family caregiver who is stressed about feeding duties?

options.A: Blaming the caregiver for the patient's poor nutritional status
options.B: Telling the caregiver to stop worrying and let the patient starve
options.C: Taking over all household chores permanently without involving family
options.D: Connecting caregivers with respite care and community support resources

explanation: Caregivers need a break too! Linking them with support and respite care helps them rest so they can continue providing great care safely.

question: Why is severe, sudden hypotension dangerous for a patient?

options.A: Sudden thickening of the heart muscle walls
options.B: Inadequate perfusion and oxygenation of vital organs
options.C: Immediate rupture of peripheral veins in the arms
options.D: Permanent blockage of the major coronary arteries

explanation: If blood pressure crashes, there isn't enough pushing power to deliver life-giving oxygen to vital organs like the brain and kidneys.

question: In nutrition, what does the acronym RDA stand for?

options.A: Required Daily Amount
options.B: Regulated Diet Acid
options.C: Recommended Dietary Allowance
options.D: Rapid Daily Assessment

explanation: RDA stands for Recommended Dietary Allowance—the daily intake level that keeps nearly all healthy people thriving.

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical concern when using health information systems?

options.A: Accidentally exposing sensitive patient data in search logs
options.B: Giving free hospital cafeteria coupons to patients
options.C: Algorithm bias that promotes low-quality research studies
options.D: Information overload from poorly filtered search results

explanation: Cafeteria coupons are unrelated to information retrieval ethics, whereas data privacy, algorithmic bias, and information overload are major concerns. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h8)

question: How should a nurse best approach a caregiver who expresses fear and hesitation about routine childhood vaccines?

options.A: Scold the parent for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Report the parent to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Listen respectfully and provide clear, reassuring education
options.D: Ignore their concerns and administer the vaccines anyway

explanation: Building trust through empathetic listening and clear, respectful communication is the most effective way to address vaccine hesitancy and correct rumors. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: Which part of the brain acts like an alarm clock to keep us physically awake?

options.A: The peripheral nervous system
options.B: The spinal cord reflex arcs
options.C: The Ascending Reticular Activating System
options.D: The cerebellum and basal ganglia

explanation: Think of the ARAS as the brain's main power switch or alarm clock, sending constant wake-up signals from the brainstem to keep the cerebral cortex alert.

question: Which statistical test should you use to compare the average scores of two completely separate groups of patients?

options.A: Descriptive median
options.B: Independent t-test
options.C: Chi-square test
options.D: Paired t-test

explanation: Spot on! When your two groups are totally separate (like Ward A patients vs. Ward B patients), an independent t-test is your go-to tool.

question: If a ward suddenly admits many new patients and uses up way more syringes and IV fluids, how are these supplies classed?

options.A: Capital costs
options.B: Variable costs
options.C: Indirect costs
options.D: Fixed costs

explanation: These are variable costs because they go up or down depending on how many patients you currently have on the ward.

question: In a centralised nursing setup, where are all the major decisions typically made?

options.A: At the individual ward level
options.B: By bedside nurses on duty
options.C: At the top executive levels
options.D: By patients and their relatives

explanation: In centralisation, power sits at the very top. Upper management or executives hold the keys to major decision-making.

question: Why must hospital infection control guidelines be updated regularly?

options.A: To give hospital administrators something to do during slow months
options.B: To match the changing fashion trends of hospital uniforms
options.C: To adapt to shifting germ behaviors and new medical evidence
options.D: To ensure old paper manuals take up more space in the storage room

explanation: Correct! Germs change and grow stronger over time, so our safety rules must keep up with new science.

question: Why is it important for a primary health nurse to understand local traditional health beliefs?

options.A: It proves that traditional practices are always superior to science
options.B: It allows the nurse to replace all modern medicine with herbs
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting local herbalists
options.D: It helps build trust and improves cooperation with medical treatments

explanation: Respecting traditional views helps nurses bridge the gap between community practices and safe, evidence-based health care. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h5)

question: Which signs are classic for a life-threatening thyroid storm?

options.A: Extremely high fever and severe tachycardia
options.B: Severe hypotension and unresponsiveness
options.C: Uncontrolled bleeding from the incision
options.D: Profound hypothermia and slow heart rate

explanation: Spot on! A thyroid storm is a medical emergency where metabolism rockets upward, causing a dangerously high fever and a racing heart.

question: Why are elderly patients much more sensitive to side effects when taking multiple drugs?

options.A: They refuse to take any form of liquid medication or syrup.
options.B: Their immune systems reject synthetic chemical compounds instantly.
options.C: They always forget to take their medications at the correct hour.
options.D: Their bodies process and clear drugs more slowly due to aging organs.

explanation: As organs age, the liver and kidneys don't clear drugs as fast. This causes medications to hang around longer and build up in the body.

question: How does human placental lactogen primarily help the developing fetus?

options.A: By directly oxygenating fetal blood within the intervillous space
options.B: By altering maternal metabolism to make more glucose available
options.C: By preventing maternal antibodies from attacking fetal tissues
options.D: By lubricating the birth canal in preparation for vaginal delivery

explanation: Placental lactogen acts as an antagonist to maternal insulin, ensuring that glucose stays in the bloodstream longer so it can readily cross over to nourish the fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h1)

question: What naturally happens to serum albumin levels when a patient's body goes through sudden inflammation?

options.A: They remain unchanged
options.B: They increase
options.C: They decrease
options.D: They fluctuate wildly

explanation: Albumin is known as a negative acute-phase reactant. When inflammation flares up, the liver slows down albumin production—good to keep in mind!

question: Why is it so important to counsel patients on what to expect physically before they take abortion medications at home?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of the hospital visit.
options.B: It legally waives the clinic from malpractice claims.
options.C: It prepares them for the expected severe cramps and heavy bleeding at home.
options.D: It prevents heavy bleeding from starting too early.

explanation: Exactly! Knowing what normal cramps and bleeding look like helps patients manage their symptoms calmly at home without unnecessary panic.

question: Which of the following is an example of resource tracking during a disaster?

options.A: Counting how many hours of sleep nurses got last night
options.B: Interviewing community leaders about past local floods
options.C: Predicting what the weather will look like next month
options.D: Monitoring available hospital beds and oxygen tank supplies

explanation: Resource tracking keeps an active count of vital physical items and space needed to care for incoming patients. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h5)

question: What does 'external validity' deal with?

options.A: How fast data goes into the hospital computer
options.B: How well patients understand their consent forms
options.C: Whether the study results can apply to other patients in the real world
options.D: How accurate the thermometers are in the laboratory

explanation: External validity asks: 'If this worked in a tiny research lab, will it also work for our patients out here on the busy hospital wards?'

question: What physical feature is an absolute must-have inside a Rapid Response Center?

options.A: Independent power generators and backup communication systems
options.B: Luxury recovery suites for high-ranking government officials
options.C: Extensive recreational facilities for off-duty emergency personnel
options.D: Permanent long-term storage for non-medical commercial goods

explanation: Disasters often knock out local electricity and phone networks. That's why backup power and comms are lifesavers to keep the center running.

question: How do telehealth and remote monitoring help keep patients out of the hospital?

options.A: By eliminating all potential health risks associated with aging at home
options.B: By allowing nurses to catch early signs of clinical deterioration and intervene quickly
options.C: By stopping clients from taking prescribed medications incorrectly
options.D: By forcing clients to visit the outpatient clinic every single day

explanation: Catching small changes early means the care team can step in and fix things before a minor issue turns into an emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical local issue at a subcutaneous injection site?

options.A: Hematoma formation
options.B: Mild local bruising
options.C: Anaphylactic shock
options.D: Sterile abscess

explanation: You've got this! Anaphylaxis is a full-body allergic reaction, not just a local problem happening right at the patch of skin where the injection went in.

question: How can a transport nurse best prepare for potential medical equipment failure during a trip?

options.A: Turn off monitors to conserve power for emergencies
options.B: Disable all battery alarms to keep the cabin quiet
options.C: Carry spare batteries and manual backup devices
options.D: Rely entirely on the vehicle's electrical system

explanation: Tech can fail us when we least expect it. Having extra batteries and manual tools like a bag-valve-mask ensures you're always ready to save the day.

question: What is the main focus of quantitative research?

options.A: Historical observation of ancient medical texts
options.B: Open-ended interviews about emotional trauma
options.C: Numerical measurement and statistical analysis
options.D: Detailed personal stories of patient suffering

explanation: Quantitative research is all about numbers, counting, and statistics. If you can measure it, it's quantitative!

question: Why is it important to involve traditional and religious leaders in health mobilisation?

options.A: They hold strong moral authority and influence public opinion
options.B: They write the national nursing curriculum
options.C: They are the only people who understand modern medicine
options.D: They are required by law to fund all local pharmacies

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are respected, and their approval helps community members trust health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h4)

question: During embryonic folding, a portion of the yolk sac is tucked inside to form which vital structure?

options.A: Amniotic cavity
options.B: Neural tube
options.C: Cardiovascular system
options.D: Primitive gut tube

explanation: Spot on! This folded tissue becomes the starting point for the baby's digestive tract, known as the primitive gut tube.

question: A patient suddenly collapses after being stung by a bee. What substance did the bee inject to cause this?

options.A: Insect venom
options.B: Bacterial toxin
options.C: Parasitic larvae
options.D: Fungal spores

explanation: Insect stings deliver venom packed with proteins that can act as powerful allergens in sensitive people.

question: In nursing research, what do we mean by a 'paradigm'?

options.A: A legal document required before treating patients
options.B: A strict mathematical formula for calculating sample size
options.C: A basic viewpoint or lens that guides how a study is approached
options.D: A specific brand of medical equipment used in hospitals

explanation: Think of a paradigm as your overall viewpoint or lens. It simply shapes how a researcher looks at a problem and decides to study it!

question: At 36 weeks, a mum is scheduled for surgery. Why must the medical team act quickly when securing her airway?

options.A: Reduced functional residual capacity leads to rapid drops in oxygen levels
options.B: Total lung capacity drops to zero once the patient lies flat
options.C: High progesterone completely paralyzes the swallow reflex instantly
options.D: The widened rib cage makes the vocal cords impossible to visualize

explanation: Mums have smaller air reserves late in pregnancy, meaning their oxygen levels can drop quicker during procedures. Excellent clinical insight!

question: An older adult in a care home suddenly becomes confused today, even though they are usually clear-headed. What should you suspect first?

options.A: Normal aging process
options.B: A developing infection
options.C: Chronic kidney failure
options.D: A high-protein diet

explanation: Great clinical instinct! In older adults, a sudden change in mental state or confusion is often the very first clue that an infection like a UTI is brewing.

question: What tends to happen when vaccination rates drop too low in a neighborhood or community?

options.A: Innate barriers become stronger to compensate
options.B: Antibody levels in newborn babies increase
options.C: Natural immunity replaces the need for shots
options.D: Outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases return

explanation: You got it! When herd immunity dips, preventable diseases find open doors to cause new outbreaks.

question: Why are medications like gabapentin or amitriptyline prescribed for some types of chronic pain?

options.A: They act as fast rescue doses for sudden, unexpected pain spikes
options.B: They replace strong opioids so the patient never develops any tolerance
options.C: They are adjuvant drugs that help calm irritated nerves and unusual pain signals
options.D: They cure the underlying tissue damage that caused the discomfort

explanation: Adjuvants are medications developed for other purposes, such as seizures or depression, that prove very effective at treating nerve-related pain. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h6)

question: When deciding on a study design, which of these is completely irrelevant?

options.A: Ethical boundaries regarding patient safety
options.B: Available financial resources and time
options.C: The specific research question being asked
options.D: The personal favorite color of the lead researcher

explanation: Haha, exactly! A researcher's favorite color has zero to do with science. Decisions are based purely on safety, questions, and resources. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary function of a Primary Care Provider (PCP) in an HMO system?

options.A: Manufacturing generic drugs for local pharmacies
options.B: Acting as the first point of contact and medical gatekeeper
options.C: Performing complex open-heart surgeries daily
options.D: Auditing the financial books of the HMO company

explanation: The PCP assesses the patient first, handles common illnesses, and decides if a specialist referral is truly necessary. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the main goal of practicing a 'Just Culture' in nursing?

options.A: Eliminating all paperwork related to patient safety incidents
options.B: Protecting the hospital from costly medical malpractice lawsuits
options.C: Encouraging staff to report errors safely without unfair blame
options.D: Ensuring every single mistake receives a harsh suspension

explanation: Fantastic! Just Culture promotes open reporting so our hospitals can learn from mistakes instead of driving them underground. You're doing great!

question: A ward manager checks how often nurses wash their hands before doing wound dressings. What kind of indicator is this?

options.A: Balancing indicator
options.B: Outcome indicator
options.C: Process indicator
options.D: Structure indicator

explanation: Hand hygiene compliance measures how care is actually being carried out. That action falls right under process indicators!

question: What is the main reason for scheduling follow-up visits after dietary counselling?

options.A: Punishing patients who failed to follow their meal plan
options.B: Re-assessing baseline anthropometric data from scratch every week
options.C: Charging additional consultation fees for hospital revenue
options.D: Monitoring progress, reviewing food logs, and adjusting goals

explanation: Right! Follow-ups let us celebrate wins, talk through struggles, and tweak the plan so it keeps working for the patient.

question: Which clinical sign is a classic indicator of respiratory distress in a newborn?

options.A: Strong, rhythmic sucking reflexes
options.B: Regular, deep, quiet breathing
options.C: A pink, warm skin appearance
options.D: Intercostal chest retractions

explanation: When a baby struggles to breathe, the skin and muscles around the ribs pull inward noticeably with each breath. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h8)

question: What happens when a patient with a weak pancreas eats a heavy, fatty meal?

options.A: All excess fat is stored safely in the liver.
options.B: Unabsorbed fats pass through, causing oily stools and cramping.
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestion permanently.
options.D: Fats instantly convert into muscle tissue.

explanation: Without enough pancreatic enzymes to break it down, fat passes right through the gut, leading to uncomfortable cramps and oily stools (steatorrhea).

question: What is the name of the Nigerian federal legislation that prohibits Female Genital Mutilation?

options.A: National Health Insurance Scheme Act
options.B: Child Rights Protection Code
options.C: Medical and Dental Practitioners Decree
options.D: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act

explanation: The VAPP Act is the primary federal law in Nigeria criminalizing harmful traditional practices, including FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h8)

question: What do we mean by the 'social determinants of health'?

options.A: The exact dosages of psychiatric prescription drugs
options.B: The specific genetic codes inherited from parents
options.C: The laboratory tests used to diagnose depression
options.D: The non-medical conditions where people live and work

explanation: Exactly! Things like where you sleep, how much you earn, and your access to school play a massive role in how healthy you are.

question: Why is the shift from paper charts to digital systems important for nurses?

options.A: It helps track patient trends and reduce errors
options.B: It slows down how quickly doctors can write new prescriptions
options.C: It removes all responsibility for charting from the nurse
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for direct patient contact

explanation: Digital systems give nurses quick access to records, making it easier to spot clinical changes and prevent mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which vitamin is especially important for building collagen during long-term wound healing?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin D

explanation: You nailed it! Vitamin C is key for making collagen, which acts like glue to heal surgical cuts.

question: What is the permanent adult name for the leftover, closed-up ductus venosus inside the liver?

options.A: Medial umbilical ligament
options.B: Ligamentum venosum
options.C: Fossa ovalis
options.D: Ligamentum teres

explanation: You've got it! Once that old fetal bypass inside the liver shuts down for good, it turns into a fibrous little band known as the ligamentum venosum.

question: What is considered the gold-standard, first-choice treatment for chronic insomnia?

options.A: High-dose benzodiazepines every night
options.B: Complete sensory deprivation therapy
options.C: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I)
options.D: Over-the-counter antihistamines

explanation: CBT-I is the top recommendation! It helps retrain your brain and sleep habits for long-term success without any risk of drug dependence.

question: Why is it wonderful for Nigerian nurses to recommend local soups like ugwu and egusi during nutrition talks?

options.A: They are affordable, culturally familiar, and rich in essential nutrients
options.B: They are the only foods allowed by traditional customs during pregnancy
options.C: They replace the need for antenatal clinic attendance
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of gestational high blood pressure

explanation: Our local soups are packed with vitamins, iron, and good fats! They are easy to find, pocket-friendly, and nourishing.

question: What is the main role of the nurse in a healthcare team working on medication adherence?

options.A: Isolating the patient from other team members to prevent conflicting advice
options.B: Taking over financial responsibilities to pay for all patient prescriptions
options.C: Acting as the central coordinator who bridges communication between the patient and team
options.D: Prescribing alternative chemical drugs when pharmacy supplies run empty

explanation: Because nurses spend the most time bedside or clinic-side, we are the vital bridge connecting the patient's reality to the rest of the healthcare team.

question: What is the 'refractory period' after ejaculation?

options.A: A period of high sympathetic activity and continuous muscle spasms
options.B: The time it takes for the internal sphincter to close
options.C: The initial phase of sperm production in the testes
options.D: A recovery time where further erection is temporarily impossible

explanation: Think of it as a normal biological timeout! The body just needs a brief resting phase before it's ready to go again.

question: How do heavy psychosocial struggles in one family member usually affect the whole household?

options.A: They lower household utility bills by reducing daily home activity
options.B: They automatically improve the communication skills of other relatives
options.C: They have no impact as long as the patient stays inside their room
options.D: They create financial strain and emotional exhaustion for everyone

explanation: Well done! Mental distress doesn't happen in a vacuum. It often leads to caregiver fatigue and puts a heavy emotional and financial load on the family.

question: What is a major long-term risk for patients dealing with ongoing autoimmune inflammation and immunosuppression?

options.A: Increased risk of cardiovascular disease and infections
options.B: Complete regeneration of destroyed organ tissue
options.C: Permanent stabilization of normal blood pressure
options.D: Total immunity against all forms of cancer

explanation: Constant inflammation wears down blood vessels over time, and medicines that lower immunity leave patients more open to infections.

question: What is the everyday clinical nickname for a bag-valve-mask device?

options.A: Suction catheter
options.B: Venturi mask
options.C: Ambu bag
options.D: Nebulizer

explanation: You will hear nurses and doctors call this the 'Ambu bag' all the time on the ward. It's your best friend in an emergency!

question: What is the typical duration of the postpartum period known as the puerperium?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: One year

explanation: The puerperium generally lasts for about six weeks after childbirth, which is the time required for maternal organs to return close to their pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: What does incidence measure in a population?

options.A: The number of new cases diagnosed
options.B: The total number of existing cases
options.C: The percentage of people who die
options.D: The cost of treating the disease

explanation: Incidence specifically counts the new diagnoses appearing over a set timeframe, showing the rate at which a disease develops. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h3)

question: How do healthcare workers usually trigger artificial active immunity in patients?

options.A: Through an emergency transfusion of donor plasma
options.B: Through the natural recovery from a severe bacterial illness
options.C: Through the application of topical antiseptic ointments
options.D: Through vaccination with weakened or killed antigens

explanation: Vaccines give your immune system a safe preview of a germ (using harmless or dead pieces), tricking it into building up long-term defense memory without getting you sick.

question: A ward manager notices missed medication doses and sloppy handovers. What is the most likely underlying issue?

options.A: Low staff morale and diminished workplace motivation
options.B: An unexpected surplus of advanced diagnostic medical equipment
options.C: Excessively high patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: Too many mandatory training workshops on patient empathy

explanation: When morale dips low, even simple daily routines like handovers can start slipping. Recognizing this helps us support one another better.

question: Why is picking the right research design so important for your everyday patient care?

options.A: It guarantees that every patient will recover quickly
options.B: It stops nurses from having to read previous literature
options.C: It ensures findings are valid and useful for patient care
options.D: It eliminates the need for any statistical data analysis

explanation: You got it! A solid design cuts down errors so the evidence we find is safe and reliable enough to use right at the bedside.

question: A community health nurse is advising local food vendors. Which safe practice should be encouraged the most?

options.A: Using expired canned goods if the metal can looks dusty
options.B: Leaving cooked rice uncovered on a table all afternoon
options.C: Rinsing raw chicken with bare hands in shared community bowls
options.D: Cooling and storing leftover perishable foods promptly

explanation: Quick refrigeration keeps leftovers out of the 'danger zone' where bacteria multiply rapidly.

question: A newly bereaved widow comes to the clinic showing deep withdrawal, sleep problems, and intense fear after going through local mourning rites. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Acute diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: Primary angle-closure glaucoma
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: The mix of trauma, harsh rituals, and isolation can easily trigger mental health struggles like PTSD and severe depression. Being able to spot this makes you a caring nurse!

question: What is the best first step if an electrical piece of emergency gear fails to turn on?

options.A: Throw the device out the window
options.B: Abandon resuscitation efforts entirely
options.C: Check the power source and cable connections
options.D: Wait for a biomedical engineer to arrive

explanation: Brilliant! Often, it's just a loose plug or unseated battery that you can fix in seconds. Always check the basics first! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: A healthy newborn is crying vigorously in the delivery room. Which circulatory change is happening to help oxygenate the blood?

options.A: Pulmonary blood vessels constrict to push blood back
options.B: Fetal shunts close to direct blood through the lungs
options.C: Systemic blood pressure drops to zero
options.D: The liver stops receiving blood supply temporarily

explanation: When the baby takes its first breath, lung vessels open up and fetal shunts close so that blood goes directly to the lungs for oxygen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of industrial pasteurization?

options.A: To destroy disease-causing microbes in liquids like milk
options.B: To remove all water from canned vegetables
options.C: To freeze liquids solid for long-term storage
options.D: To add artificial colors and flavors to beverages

explanation: Pasteurization uses gentle heat to knock out dangerous germs in everyday drinks like milk without ruining the taste or quality.

question: What must a nurse check before giving fluids to someone who just had surgery?

options.A: Testing the patient's long-term memory function
options.B: Checking for the presence of bowel sounds
options.C: Assessing the patient's skin color on the lower extremities
options.D: Measuring the patient's exact daily walking distance

explanation: Listening for bowel sounds tells you if the gut has woken up from anesthesia and is ready to process anything.

question: What is the main job of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy?

options.A: To signal the corpus luteum to continue producing progesterone
options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure during the first trimester
options.C: To prepare the fetal lungs for air breathing
options.D: To stimulate milk production in the maternal mammary glands

explanation: Wonderful! hCG is the famous pregnancy hormone that tells the ovary's corpus luteum to keep pumping out progesterone until the placenta is ready to take over.

question: A patient has trouble swallowing (dysphagia) after a stroke. What kind of fluids are they likely given?

options.A: Thickened liquids to prevent choking and aspiration
options.B: Completely clear water to test immediate swallowing speed
options.C: Unrestricted fluids served through a wide straw
options.D: Hot liquids to stimulate throat nerve endings

explanation: Thin water runs down too fast for weak throat muscles. Thickened liquids travel slower, giving the patient time to swallow safely without choking.

question: A nurse makes a medication calculation error because orientation on the new infusion pump was rushed. What is the root cause?

options.A: Lack of knowledge or training
options.B: Willful defiance of hospital policy
options.C: An intentional desire to cause harm
options.D: Personal substance abuse issues

explanation: When a nurse makes a mistake due to poor orientation, the primary issue is a lack of proper training. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h4)

question: A doctor orders IV glucose for a suspected Wernicke patient. What should you check first?

options.A: Warm the IV bag to room temperature
options.B: Confirm that thiamine has already been given
options.C: Check the patient's blood pressure every 5 minutes
options.D: Ask if they want fruit juice instead

explanation: Brilliant! Always verify that thiamine went in first to protect the patient's brain from crashing when glucose is introduced.

question: A nurse is assessing a patient who uses a wheelchair full-time. Which oversight represents a common mistake in clinical practice?

options.A: Failing to check routine preventative screenings like blood pressure and dental health
options.B: Asking the patient about their daily routine for bathing and dressing
options.C: Evaluating the patient for chronic muscle spasms and nerve pain
options.D: Inspecting the skin over the sacrum and heels for early redness

explanation: Clinicians often fixate on the visible disability and neglect general preventative healthcare that all patients require. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h2)

question: What happens when healthcare workers operate in isolated silos within a community?

options.A: Treatment plans become much easier for patients to follow
options.B: Every professional automatically knows what the others are doing
options.C: Patient care becomes fragmented and important details are missed
options.D: Healthcare costs drop significantly for local families

explanation: Spot on! Working in isolation means communication breaks down, leaving gaps that can hurt patient care.

question: What is the main way ordinary Nigerians pay for their healthcare needs?

options.A: Community health funds
options.B: Federal health insurance
options.C: Out-of-pocket payments
options.D: Employer-paid retainerships

explanation: You got it! Most Nigerians pay cash straight from their pockets for every consultation, lab test, and prescription whenever they visit a clinic.

question: How do research objectives connect to your main research question?

options.A: Objectives replace the research question entirely during data analysis
options.B: Objectives are guesses made before looking at the research question
options.C: Objectives explain why the research question is impossible to answer
options.D: Objectives break the main question down into smaller, actionable steps

explanation: Think of objectives as the stepping stones. They take your big main research question and slice it into smaller, bite-sized goals you can achieve one by one.

question: Your IV patient suddenly feels short of breath, has crackles in their lungs, and high blood pressure. What do you do first?

options.A: Slow the infusion rate, elevate the head of the bed, and notify the provider
options.B: Flush the line rapidly with a bolus of normal saline to check patency
options.C: Place the client flat on their left side and prepare for emergency intubation
options.D: Remove the IV cannula immediately and apply a cold ice pack to the limb

explanation: Classic signs of fluid overload! Slowing the fluids and sitting the patient up helps them breathe easier while you alert the doctor.

question: What usually happens to public health funding when the national economy goes through a tough patch?

options.A: Private clinics take over all public patients
options.B: Hospitals receive a sudden surge of extra grants
options.C: The cost of medical care drops to zero everywhere
options.D: Government health budgets are often reduced

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight nationally, governments collect less revenue and unfortunately tend to slash public sector budgets, including healthcare.

question: What does a null hypothesis usually state?

options.A: There is a strong positive effect from the treatment
options.B: There is no relationship between the variables
options.C: The sample size is too small to complete the study
options.D: The research question was poorly written

explanation: The null hypothesis is the 'no difference' or 'no effect' guess. It assumes any change you see is just by chance!

question: A patient with severe internal bleeding from a car crash is most likely to develop which type of shock?

options.A: Neurogenic shock
options.B: Hypovolemic shock
options.C: Anaphylactic shock
options.D: Cardiogenic shock

explanation: Hypovolemic shock is caused by a drastic loss of blood volume circulating in the body. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h5)

question: A community health nurse wants to lower malaria cases in a rural Nigerian village. Which action is the most practical primary health care step?

options.A: Stopping all routine vaccinations until malaria is completely eradicated
options.B: Admitting every healthy villager into the central hospital for observation
options.C: Waiting until an epidemic is declared before taking any action at all
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated bed nets and teaching mothers how to use them

explanation: Giving out bed nets and showing families how to use them directly protects people from nightly mosquito bites right in their homes. Excellent community nursing in action!

question: What is a crucial pre-procedure assessment step if the CT scan involves intravenous contrast?

options.A: Placing a urinary catheter for the scan
options.B: Checking the patient for latex allergies
options.C: Checking kidney function blood tests
options.D: Administering a full dose of oral laxatives

explanation: Iodinated contrast media is cleared by the kidneys, so nurses must check kidney function values like serum creatinine before the procedure to prevent contrast-induced kidney injury. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which family planning method category also helps protect against Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal pills
options.B: Barrier methods
options.C: Permanent surgeries
options.D: Intrauterine devices

explanation: Only barrier methods like condoms physically block fluids, which stops both unwanted pregnancy AND pesky STIs. Pills and IUDs do not protect against infections!

question: What does the nursing abbreviation MSE stand for?

options.A: Medical Symptom Evaluation
options.B: Mental Stability Evaluation
options.C: Mental Status Examination
options.D: Mood State Estimator

explanation: MSE stands for Mental Status Examination. It's a quick, structured way nurses and doctors check how a patient is thinking, feeling, and functioning right now.

question: How does the World Wide Web relate to the internet?

options.A: It is an older offline system replaced by the internet
options.B: It is a standalone computer used only by doctors
options.C: It is a specific service that displays web pages using the internet
options.D: It is the physical wire running underneath hospital floors

explanation: The web is just one part of the internet, acting as a collection of pages and sites viewed through a browser. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h1)

question: A student nurse is getting ready to irrigate an eye. Which action means they need a quick correction?

options.A: Placing a waterproof towel and a kidney basin under the cheek
options.B: Encouraging the patient to blink periodically during the wash
options.C: Resting fingers directly upon the patient's eyeball to hold it open
options.D: Holding the irrigation tubing about one inch away from the eye

explanation: Ouch! Always rest your fingers on the bony cheekbone or forehead, never directly on the eyeball, to prevent accidental pressure injury.

question: What is a frequent danger for the baby when a mother experiences a significant placental abruption?

options.A: Rapid acceleration of normal fetal skeletal growth
options.B: Hypoxia and acute distress due to reduced oxygen transfer
options.C: Delayed closure of the fetal heart shunts after delivery
options.D: Permanent discoloration of the newborn's skin at birth

explanation: When the placenta prematurely detaches, the surface area for gas exchange shrinks drastically, starving the fetus of oxygen. You are mastering key obstetric concepts!

question: Why can predictive formulas (like the Harris-Benedict equation) sometimes be misleading for critically ill patients?

options.A: They measure direct body heat rather than gas exchange
options.B: They require the patient to be placed inside a sealed heat chamber
options.C: They only provide estimates and may miscalculate actual needs during severe illness
options.D: They can only be used on healthy newborn infants

explanation: Formulas use averages for healthy people. But when a patient has severe burns or trauma, their body behaves unpredictably, so formulas can miss the mark.

question: Which government program became the main payer for long-term nursing home care after 1965?

options.A: Medicare
options.B: The Hill-Burton fund
options.C: Social Security
options.D: Medicaid

explanation: Medicaid was built to support low-income individuals, and over time it grew to become the primary financial backbone paying for long-term stays in nursing facilities.

question: A patient is brought to the emergency unit looking very restless, sweating profusely, and with a racing heart after taking an unknown substance. Which drug class is likely to blame?

options.A: Opioids
options.B: Sedative-hypnotics
options.C: Barbiturates
options.D: Stimulants

explanation: Think of stimulants as overcharging the body's 'fight or flight' system—driving up the heart rate, causing heavy sweating, and making the patient jittery or agitated.

question: An EPS report shows dangerous heart rhythms that couldn't be fixed with ablation. What might the medical team look at next?

options.A: Preparing the patient for discussion about an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
options.B: Removing all cardiac monitoring equipment permanently
options.C: Scheduling an immediate open-heart surgery for valve replacement
options.D: Discharging the patient with no further restrictions or medications

explanation: When an abnormal pathway can't be successfully ablated away, an implantable device (like an ICD) is often the next line of defense to keep the patient safe from sudden cardiac arrest.

question: Which agency checks public procurement processes in Nigeria to ensure everything is transparent?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Bureau of Public Procurement
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) sets rules and monitors government contracts to keep the process open and honest.

question: What is the incubation period of an infectious disease?

options.A: The period between receiving a vaccine and gaining immunity
options.B: The duration a patient remains infectious after recovery
options.C: The time between pathogen entry and the first symptom
options.D: The exact number of days a patient stays in the hospital

explanation: The incubation period starts when germs enter the body and ends when the very first signs of sickness appear. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h1)

question: What is the usual daily fat limit for a strict low-fat therapeutic diet?

options.A: Exactly zero grams per day
options.B: Less than 20 grams per day
options.C: Around 70 to 100 grams daily
options.D: Up to 50 percent of total calories

explanation: You got this! A strict low-fat diet keeps fat under 20 grams daily. Eating completely zero fat is almost impossible with natural foods.

question: Why are temporary leave policies considered clinical interventions rather than just rewards?

options.A: They allow the hospital to permanently reduce bed capacity
options.B: They actively test the patient's coping and medication management skills outside the hospital
options.C: They prove to the court that the patient no longer needs medication
options.D: They force family members to take over full financial responsibility

explanation: Think of leave as a practical test! It helps us see how well a patient handles daily life and takes their medications outside the hospital walls.

question: Which of these best describes permanent harm?

options.A: A temporary drop in blood pressure after changing positions
options.B: A lasting disability or loss of function caused by an error
options.C: A mild headache that resolves after sleeping overnight
options.D: An allergic rash that disappears after taking an antihistamine

explanation: Permanent harm means the patient suffers a long-term or irreversible loss of ability. This is why our daily safety checks are so important.

question: Your clinic has free cholera vaccines, but villagers are refusing them because of scary rumours. What should you do?

options.A: Close the clinic permanently and transfer the nursing staff to a city
options.B: Use BCC strategies like town hall meetings to address rumors and build trust
options.C: Call the police to force every single villager to receive the injection
options.D: Ignore the rumours and wait for people to figure out the truth alone

explanation: Exactly! Open dialogue and town hall meetings help clear up dangerous myths and build confidence in public health care.

question: What is a big plus of having homestead gardens in rural areas?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any community health education
options.B: Generating large profits on international export markets
options.C: Providing immediate access to fresh vegetables and fruits
options.D: Replacing local health clinics with herbal gardens

explanation: You got it! Homestead gardens mean families can just walk to their backyard to grab fresh, nutritious greens without needing extra cash or long travel.

question: What does it mean to confuse correlation with causation in healthcare?

options.A: Assuming one event caused another just because they happened together
options.B: Failing to record patient vital signs in the electronic health record
options.C: Comparing infection rates between two completely different hospitals
options.D: Using the wrong chart type to present monthly admission numbers

explanation: Spot on! Just because two things happen at the same time doesn't mean one caused the other. Always dig deeper!

question: What do not-for-profit health organizations do with any extra money they make?

options.A: Transfer it directly to government tax accounts
options.B: Distribute it equally among private shareholders as dividends
options.C: Reinvest it into facility improvement and patient care
options.D: Hold it in offshore bank accounts for future business ventures

explanation: You got it! Not-for-profit centers put every extra naira right back into upgrading their equipment and helping the community.

question: What event usually triggers an immediate public health outbreak investigation?

options.A: An annual audit of the hospital electricity bill
options.B: The routine retirement of a senior hospital administrator
options.C: The delivery of new office furniture to the clinic
options.D: A sudden jump in disease cases above the normal level

explanation: When we suddenly see way more sick people than we normally expect in an area, that's our cue to investigate right away!

question: Why must nurses emphasize treating sexual partners when a teenager is diagnosed with a bacterial STI?

options.A: To prevent reinfection of the original patient and control community spread
options.B: To ensure the laboratory technicians have enough test samples
options.C: To fulfill mandatory legal requirements for school attendance
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing antibiotics

explanation: Spot on! Treating partners stops the 'ping-pong' effect where partners pass the infection right back to each other.

question: Why is it super important for a nurse researcher to clearly define their study population?

options.A: It ensures that every person in the country gets surveyed
options.B: It eliminates all possible errors in data collection
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of printing research papers
options.D: It helps them know exactly who the final study results will apply to

explanation: Spot on! When you know your exact population, you can proudly say who your findings will help in everyday hospital or community practice.

question: In the nursing process, what is the evaluation step used to find out?

options.A: Which nurse gets assigned to night shift duty
options.B: Whether patient goals and outcomes have been met
options.C: How much the patient's hospital bill will cost
options.D: What medications the doctor should prescribe next

explanation: Evaluation is your final check in the nursing process to see if your care plan actually helped the patient reach their health goals.

question: Which question is a patient in the anger stage most likely to ask?

options.A: How much will this treatment cost?
options.B: When will my test results arrive?
options.C: Can we negotiate more time?
options.D: Why is this happening to me?

explanation: Anger comes from deep hurt and the feeling of unfairness, making patients ask 'Why me?'

question: Why do many families in Nigeria first take a relative showing acute psychosis to spiritual or traditional healers?

options.A: Orthodox psychiatric nurses refuse to admit community members
options.B: Traditional healers offer free prescription psychiatric medications
options.C: Spiritual homes are always located closer than primary health centers
options.D: Cultural beliefs often attribute mental illness to spiritual causes

explanation: Culture shapes health! Many communities view sudden mental health changes through a spiritual lens, which naturally guides where they go for help first.

question: What is a key question a nurse can ask to assess food security in a patient?

options.A: What is your exact family income down to the last dollar?
options.B: Do you prefer eating white bread or whole grain bread?
options.C: Do you worry about running out of food before getting more money?
options.D: How many hours of physical exercise do you do each week?

explanation: Screening for food security involves asking direct, simple questions about running out of food and lacking money to buy more. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention strategies for a patient?

options.A: Preventing any future contact between the host and the environment
options.B: Rehabilitating a patient after permanent disability has occurred
options.C: Eliminating the vector species completely from a tropical region
options.D: Detecting and treating an infection early before it causes severe illness

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching things early! Think of screenings and prompt treatments that stop a small infection from turning into a major emergency.

question: Why is it so important for nurses to routinely check cranial nerves linked to the special senses?

options.A: Changes in sensory function can indicate early brain injury or increased pressure
options.B: It replaces the need for measuring blood pressure and pulse
options.C: It proves whether the patient is following a healthy daily diet
options.D: It prevents the patient from developing normal age-related hearing loss

explanation: Because cranial nerves plug right into the brain, a sudden change in someone's vision, hearing, or pupil reaction can be an early warning sign that pressure inside the skull is rising.

question: Why is a flatus tube generally left in place for only a short period, such as 20 to 30 minutes?

options.A: To ensure the tube does not dissolve inside the bowel
options.B: To prevent the kidneys from stopping urine output
options.C: To prevent pressure damage to the delicate rectal lining
options.D: To stop the patient from drinking too much water

explanation: Prolonged pressure from an indwelling tube can compromise blood flow to the rectal mucosa, leading to irritation, ulceration, or necrosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement in nursing?

options.A: Making patient care safer and more reliable
options.B: Reducing the total number of employed nurses
options.C: Punishing staff members who make mistakes
options.D: Increasing the cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Great job! Quality improvement is all about making healthcare better and safer for our patients, rather than pointing fingers. You've got this!

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do before starting a community health project?

options.A: Accurately assessing the true health needs of the community
options.B: Purchasing expensive medical equipment for the local clinic
options.C: Drafting strict new health laws for the national parliament
options.D: Hiring international consultants to run the program

explanation: You nailed it. Always check what the community actually needs first, so you don't waste time and energy solving the wrong problems!

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.A: Digest nutrients and absorb water
options.B: Filter waste and produce urine
options.C: Pump blood through the pelvic floor
options.D: Produce eggs and secrete sex hormones

explanation: Ovaries serve as both glands that make hormones (estrogen and progesterone) and storage sites for female eggs. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of regular pacemaker interrogation appointments?

options.A: To surgically replace the battery every six months
options.B: To reprogram the heart muscle to beat much faster
options.C: To check battery life and evaluate device functioning
options.D: To wash the surgical scar and apply fresh bandages

explanation: Interrogation allows healthcare providers to assess remaining battery power, lead performance, and device data. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of emergency nursing when managing a life-threatening condition?

options.A: Conducting routine diagnostic laboratory tests
options.B: Completing a full health history before acting
options.C: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.D: Rapid identification and immediate intervention

explanation: Emergency nursing focuses on acting fast to save lives when a patient's condition can quickly deteriorate. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h1)

question: How does family planning directly help safe motherhood efforts?

options.A: By eliminating all natural causes of infertility
options.B: By helping women space pregnancies to protect their physical recovery
options.C: By ensuring women have children as rapidly as possible
options.D: By replacing the need for antenatal clinic attendance

explanation: Spacing kids gives mum's body a well-deserved break to build back her blood levels and strength before the next journey.

question: Which type of facility usually provides secondary level healthcare services?

options.A: General hospitals
options.B: Teaching hospitals
options.C: Traditional herbal shops
options.D: Primary health centres

explanation: Well done! General hospitals step in when patients need doctors who specialize in specific areas, minor surgeries, or admission beyond what a primary health center can handle.

question: What is the main meaning of 'food insecurity'?

options.A: Temporary fasting practiced during religious or cultural holiday seasons
options.B: A personal choice to go on a strict weight-loss diet for health reasons
options.C: Lack of consistent access to enough safe and nutritious food for a healthy life
options.D: Having too many grocery stores in a single neighborhood community

explanation: Food insecurity means a person or family never quite knows where their next wholesome meal is coming from.

question: Which of these actions is NOT recommended when caring for a patient taking broad-spectrum antibiotics?

options.A: Practicing thorough hand hygiene before and after entering the patient's room
options.B: Discontinuing the prescribed antibiotic early as soon as the patient feels better
options.C: Monitoring the patient closely for signs of secondary fungal or bacterial overgrowth
options.D: Educating the patient about eating probiotic-rich foods or yogurt if permitted

explanation: Never stop antibiotics early! Doing so lets stronger germs survive and bounce back. Always encourage patients to finish their full dose while you keep an eye out for opportunistic infections.

question: What are the three main pillars that make up evidence-based practice?

options.A: Patient age, family background, and disease diagnosis
options.B: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values
options.C: Hospital policy, physician orders, and insurance budgets
options.D: Textbook theory, nursing tradition, and administrative rules

explanation: EBP is a balanced approach that requires combining valid research findings with the nurse's professional judgment and what matters to the patient. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is it smart to do quick stretches during natural pauses, like waiting for a computer system to load?

options.A: It is the only legal time management allows for stretching
options.B: It integrates injury prevention seamlessly into the existing workflow
options.C: It prevents the computer hardware from crashing unexpectedly
options.D: It doubles the processing speed of electronic health records

explanation: Spot on! Using your downtime for a quick stretch ensures you actually take care of your body despite a crazy busy schedule. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of HIV counselling?

options.A: To enable the client to cope with stress and make personal decisions
options.B: To force patients to reveal their status to family members immediately
options.C: To diagnose opportunistic infections without laboratory tests
options.D: To register patients for mandatory government employment schemes

explanation: HIV counselling provides a safe space for clients to process emotions and make informed choices about their health. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h1)

question: Which complication is a major risk for clients taking long-term oral NSAIDs for osteoarthritis pain?

options.A: Sudden uncontrollable weight loss and high fever
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of new joint cartilage
options.C: Gastrointestinal bleeding and stomach ulcers
options.D: Permanent darkening of the skin and hair

explanation: Oral NSAIDs block protective stomach lining chemicals, putting regular users at high risk for ulcers and bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)

question: What causes moral distress for a primary health care nurse?

options.A: Having too many administrative meetings with government officials
options.B: Receiving regular feedback from satisfied community members
options.C: Knowing the correct patient care needed but lacking the resources to deliver it
options.D: Working standard daytime hours in a rural health post

explanation: Moral distress happens when a nurse knows the right clinical action to take but systemic shortages prevent them from doing it. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is a great quality to look for when picking members for a QI team?

options.A: Preference for keeping current hospital routines unchanged
options.B: High seniority status and administrative authority only
options.C: Curiosity about how things work and respect from peers
options.D: Experience working exclusively on the night shift

explanation: Spot on! Good team members need open minds to question old routines and enough respect from coworkers to get others on board.

question: A client with severe high blood pressure requests a combined oral contraceptive pill. What is the most appropriate nursing action based on safety guidelines?

options.A: Dispense the pills immediately to respect her personal autonomy and choice
options.B: Double the normal starting dose to make sure the pills work effectively
options.C: Tell her to stop checking her blood pressure while taking the hormonal medication
options.D: Suggest an alternative safe method because combined pills pose high cardiovascular risks here

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives can worsen hypertension and increase stroke risks, making them medically restricted for this client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: If thyroid hormone levels in the blood get very high, what happens to thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) from the pituitary?

options.A: TSH release remains completely unchanged
options.B: TSH release decreases due to negative feedback
options.C: TSH release stops entirely and permanently
options.D: TSH release increases to match thyroid hormone levels

explanation: When there is already plenty of thyroid hormone around, the pituitary gets the memo and slows down its TSH output so you don't overheat!

question: What kind of information does qualitative data primarily capture?

options.A: Standardized monitoring device readouts and scores
options.B: Exact physical weights and chemical lab values
options.C: Precise mathematical frequencies and statistical averages
options.D: Human experiences, feelings, and descriptive narratives

explanation: Qualitative data focuses on words and stories that explain what a healthcare experience feels like to a patient. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why does a lack of financial transparency harm grassroots health committees?

options.A: It destroys community trust and discourages local donations and participation
options.B: It causes international pharmaceutical companies to raise drug prices
options.C: It forces health workers to close all clinics permanently
options.D: It automatically stops the federal government from paying nurse salaries

explanation: When villagers suspect mismanagement of local health funds, they lose faith in the committee and refuse to support health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which digital tool is commonly used to send quick appointment reminders straight to a pregnant client's phone?

options.A: SMS text messages
options.B: Megaphone broadcasts
options.C: Flannel graphs
options.D: Printed paper posters

explanation: Simple SMS text messages land directly on personal phones, making them a super convenient way to remind clients not to miss their antenatal visits.

question: What term describes the heavy emotional stress and guilt a health worker feels after being involved in a patient safety incident?

options.A: Second victim syndrome
options.B: Professional burnout
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: Compassion fatigue

explanation: It sounds heavy, but 'second victim syndrome' is very real. Clinicians who experience a tragic accident often need a lot of support and compassion too.

question: When checking a patient's standing posture from behind, what is the first thing a nurse should look for?

options.A: Symmetry of the shoulders and hips
options.B: The strength of the hand grip
options.C: The speed of the patient's heart rate
options.D: The exact color of the patient's eyes

explanation: By checking if both shoulders and hips line up evenly, you can quickly spot early signs of spinal curves like scoliosis.

question: Which group of medications is well-known for damaging hearing (ototoxicity)?

options.A: H2 receptor antagonists
options.B: Aminoglycoside antibiotics
options.C: Short-acting nitrates
options.D: Inhaled corticosteroids

explanation: Watch out for aminoglycoside antibiotics! They can sometimes harm the inner ear and lead to hearing problems if not monitored closely.

question: Why do nursing students need to learn about different sources of knowledge?

options.A: To eliminate the need for clinical experience entirely
options.B: To memorize every historical medical text ever written
options.C: To understand why clinical guidelines change and why evidence matters
options.D: To learn how to diagnose patients without a doctor

explanation: Knowing where knowledge comes from helps you see why nursing care changes for the better as new evidence comes to light. You've got this!

question: What is an important public health fact about many common vision and hearing problems?

options.A: Most sensory losses happen suddenly without any warning.
options.B: They are rarely linked to chronic systemic illnesses.
options.C: A large percentage of cases can be prevented.
options.D: They only affect individuals over the age of eighty.

explanation: You'll be glad to know that many vision and hearing issues can actually be prevented through healthy habits and early care. Public health data proves we can stop a lot of sensory loss before it even starts!

question: In healthcare technology, what is the main goal of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)?

options.A: Writing new programming code for hospital databases
options.B: Teaching computer science classes to student nurses
options.C: How clinicians interact with digital technology during work
options.D: Repairing broken computer hardware in the hospital ward

explanation: You got this! HCI is simply about how healthcare workers use digital tools on the job, making sure technology helps rather than frustrates you.

question: Which tiny bone in the middle ear is attached directly to the eardrum?

options.A: Incus
options.B: Cochlea
options.C: Stapes
options.D: Malleus

explanation: The malleus (also known as the hammer) rests right against the eardrum to catch its first vibrations.

question: A patient is prescribed a metered-dose inhaler without a spacer and complains that the medicine just hits their throat. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Instruct the patient to hold their breath for five minutes after inhaling
options.B: Call the doctor to change the prescription to a skin patch
options.C: Advise the patient to obtain and use a spacer device to improve drug delivery
options.D: Tell the patient to swallow the medicine instead of breathing it in

explanation: Spacers act as a holding chamber that slows down the spray, preventing medication from depositing in the mouth and throat instead of the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: During a building collapse with dozens of victims, a patient with severe, fatal injuries gets an expectant (black) tag. Why do we do this?

options.A: Because nurses are not legally allowed to touch trauma patients outdoors
options.B: To preserve scarce medical supplies for victims who have a better chance of survival
options.C: Because minor injuries always take legal precedence over head trauma
options.D: To punish the patient for not wearing safety equipment

explanation: This is one of the hardest parts of nursing, but when supplies are limited, we must focus our efforts where we can genuinely save lives.

question: True informed consent in reproductive health is best described as which of the following?

options.A: An optional form that clients can sign without reading
options.B: An ongoing dialogue between the client and the nurse
options.C: A quick signature collected right before a surgical procedure
options.D: A decision made entirely by the doctor without client input

explanation: Correct! Informed consent isn't just a paper signature—it's a continuous conversation ensuring the patient truly understands and agrees to their care plan.

question: A patient arrives pale, dizzy, and bleeding heavily after an unsafe abortion. What action should you take right away?

options.A: Perform a complete pelvic exam without checking vital signs
options.B: Start a large-bore intravenous line for fluid resuscitation
options.C: Ask the patient to write down a detailed confession of the act
options.D: Wait for the attending physician to arrive before acting

explanation: You got this! When someone is bleeding heavily, getting IV access fast is crucial to restore fluids, boost blood volume, and prevent shock.

question: If a study shows a significant link between long shifts and nurse burnout, what is the best takeaway for hospital managers?

options.A: Increase shift lengths further to test the null hypothesis again
options.B: Dismiss the finding because statistical tests never apply to real hospitals
options.C: Review and adjust staff shift scheduling policies to reduce burnout
options.D: Switch all patient data collection methods to continuous numerical scales

explanation: Spot on! Research is meant to guide practical changes that improve staff well-being and patient safety in our hospitals.

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) counselling?

options.A: To punish clients who break hospital rules
options.B: To force clients to speak with law enforcement
options.C: To support clients physically and emotionally
options.D: To convince clients to change their religious beliefs

explanation: PAC counselling is all about giving compassionate physical and emotional support to help your client heal safely. As a nurse, creating a safe space makes all the difference! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h1)

question: An angry nursing student wants to yell at a strict clinical instructor, but instead channels that energy into scrubbing the skill lab for hours. What defense mechanism is this?

options.A: Sublimation
options.B: Projection
options.C: Regression
options.D: Denial

explanation: That is sublimation! It is taking raw, unacceptable aggression and turning it into something super productive and socially acceptable. Cleaning counts as a win!

question: How long must symptoms last before a doctor or nurse can clinically diagnose female sexual dysfunction?

options.A: At least six months
options.B: At least two weeks
options.C: Twelve months straight
options.D: One month or more

explanation: You've got this! Because temporary stress happens to everyone, clinicians look for symptoms to last at least six months along with personal distress before making a diagnosis.

question: What is the main way drugs are grouped by their origin?

options.A: The specific disease they are used to treat
options.B: The route used to administer the medication
options.C: The exact cost of manufacturing the drug
options.D: Their original source and how they are made

explanation: You'll often see drugs grouped by where they come from—whether they're naturally found in plants or animals, dug from minerals, or built in a lab!

question: Why do modern surgical wards prefer closed drainage systems over open ones?

options.A: They completely stop the patient from feeling any surgical pain
options.B: They significantly lower the risk of outside bacteria entering the body
